verdict.rationale: Fly.io's own marketing says Fly Machines boot in under a second and "scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives." Its docs also mention idle stop/wake-on-request behavior, but no documented load-based autoscaling mechanism (metrics, thresholds, policies) is shown; `fly scale` is a manual command. Missing for 10: documentation of automatic load-based scaling triggers and configuration, evidence of burst absorption in practice, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can rely on load-based autoscaling to absorb large traffic bursts automatically

citations.quote: Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users, and scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives.
Host a remote MCP server on a Fly Machine that any MCP client can reach over HTTP and that stops when idle
